Reporting Errors

When an AI tool gets something wrong, tell me. Here is who to reach and why it matters more than you might think.
Required before first use
Required Reading

The AI tools you use for School Tech work are things I build and maintain. When one gets something wrong, I don't see it unless you tell me. So tell me.

Reach out to Adam. Email is best.
That's the whole process. You know who I am - no ticket, no form, no special wording. Send me an email describing what went wrong.

Why this matters

An error you don't report is an error that never gets fixed. I can only correct what I know about, and I'm not watching over your shoulder while you work. A quick email is the difference between a problem that gets solved and one that keeps happening to you and to everyone else using the same tool.

Don't assume someone else already said something. Most of the time, nobody has. The thing that feels too small to mention is usually exactly the thing I'd want to know.

The three-times rule

Here is the clearest signal that it's time to email me:

If you're correcting the same thing more than three times, reach out. When you find yourself fixing the same mistake over and over - the tool keeps getting one fact wrong, keeps using the wrong format, keeps missing the same step - that's not something you should have to keep patching by hand.

When you flag a repeat problem like that, I can correct it inside the AI itself - in the instructions the tool runs on - so it stops happening for good. Fix it once at the source instead of a hundred times in your day.

What to put in the email

Nothing formal. Just enough that I can see what you saw:

1
Which tool
The name of the project, chat, or skill you were using.
2
What went wrong
What you expected versus what it actually did. A sentence is fine.
3
Whether it's a repeat
Tell me if this is the same thing you've had to correct before. That moves it to the top of my list.
A screenshot or a copy of the conversation helps but it isn't required. Send what you have.
The short version: something's wrong, email Adam. Correcting it three times? Email Adam. If you don't tell me, it never gets fixed.
